parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The equation for the reduction of iron(III) oxide by carbon monoxide at $450^{\circ}\text{C}$ is shown.

$$\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3(\text{s}) + 3\text{CO}(\text{g}) \rightarrow 2\text{Fe}(\text{s}) + 3\text{CO}_2(\text{g}) \hspace{2em} \Delta G^{\ominus} = -36.2\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

Table 3.1 shows the enthalpy of formation, $\Delta H_{\text{f}}^{\ominus}$, and the entropy, $S^{\ominus}$, for some substances.

Table 3.1

|  | $\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3(\text{s})$ | $\text{CO}(\text{g})$ | $\text{Fe}(\text{s})$ | $\text{CO}_2(\text{g})$ |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| $\Delta H_{\text{f}}^{\ominus} / \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ | $-824.2$ | $-110.5$ | $0.0$ | $-393.5$ |
| $S^{\ominus} / \text{J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$ | $87.4$ | to be calculated | $27.3$ | $213.8$ |

Use the data in Table 3.1 to calculate the entropy, $S^{\ominus}$, of carbon monoxide at $450^{\circ}\text{C}$.

Show your working.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Iron(II) oxide can also be reduced to iron by carbon monoxide, as shown.

$$\text{FeO}(\text{s}) + \text{CO}(\text{g}) \rightarrow \text{Fe}(\text{s}) + \text{CO}_2(\text{g}) \hspace{2em} \Delta H^{\ominus} = -11.1\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$
$$\Delta S^{\ominus} = -15.2\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$$

State the effect of increasing temperature on the feasibility of this reaction.

Explain your answer.
